propositions: A raising LLM call leaves run() via interpret_failure re-raising before record() is reached, so no usage row is written for the failed call.
JSONL spend totals folded by summarize() silently under-report actual spend by exactly the failed calls, affecting billable CI job summaries.
Per-step attribution cannot see failed calls, so expensive retry-to-exhaustion failures are unattributable.
A failed call should write a usage row with identifying fields (op, step, model_class, model, provider) plus known token counters, explicitly distinguishable from a successful row.
Recording on the failure path must not convert or swallow the original provider exception, and must avoid double-counting a call that fails and is then retried.
A real Bedrock run with an invalid model id produced five healthy rows and no rows for the two failed passes (verify, coach).
